question: E3 cross-model pairs: E3 found that collaborating adopted alone pays its user on gpt-6-luna (+5.7 to +7.4) and not on claude-sonnet-5-5 (-0.8, the partner +2.6). Is that the partner's strength (a default partner that finds the frontier alone leaves nothing for the rule to add) or the adopter's own model? A luna agent and a sonnet agent play each other on E1's 40 instances, each of the two models with and without a strategy, in both seats.

instances.note: E1's test set; the same-model twins are E3's luna control and sonnet arms

cells: 16 per arm (the rule diagonal and every strategy against neutral in both seats), two arms with the seats' models swapped: 1,280 games, 640 with a rule on the luna side and 640 with a rule on the sonnet side
analysis: Paired by instance (exact sign tests) against the arm's own mixed default pair, with the two arms pooled by model (seat 1 of one arm and seat 2 of the other play the same model), 80 games per direction when both arms are played; the same-model twins are E3's luna control and sonnet arms on the same 40 instances.

cross_luna_sonnet.model_condition: seat 1 gpt-6-luna (OpenAI, reasoning off), seat 2 claude-sonnet-5-5 (proxy, thinking off)
cross_luna_sonnet.prediction: see predictions in the arm's config

cross_sonnet_luna.prediction: see predictions in the arm's config

predictions.neutral_pair: In the mixed default pair sonnet's agent takes at least 5 points more than luna's, and the pair's joint payoff lies between the two same-model default pairs (130.0 for luna at the default temperature, 138.1 for sonnet, E3).
predictions.collaborating_alone: Partner-strength account (ours): luna's collaborating rule against sonnet's default agent does not pay luna (own gain within 3 points of its payoff in the mixed default pair; the joint payoff rises and the gain goes to sonnet), while sonnet's collaborating rule against luna's default agent pays sonnet (+3 or more, p < .05), because luna cannot find the frontier alone. The alternative, that the adopter's own model decides, predicts the opposite pattern (luna gains as in E1, sonnet does not as in E3).
predictions.competing_alone: sonnet competing against luna's default agent takes at least 8 points from luna (in E1 a competing luna took 11.6 from it) and gains itself (+3 or more); luna competing against sonnet's default agent gains nothing (within 3 points) and takes under 5.
predictions.symmetric: Collaborating pairs are the best symmetric cell and competing pairs the worst in both arms; the mixed collaborating pair's joint payoff is at least luna's own collaborating pair's (136.8) and the mixed default pair's.
predictions.soft_alone: Compromising, accommodating and avoiding adopted alone lose for whichever model adopts them, and lose more when the partner is sonnet than when it is luna.
predictions.analysis: Paired by instance (exact sign tests) against the arm's own mixed default pair, with the two arms pooled by model (seat 1 of one arm and seat 2 of the other play the same model), 80 games per direction when both arms are played; the same-model twins are E3's luna control and sonnet arms on the same 40 instances.
